passage:
Sports day. Worst day.
I was sure I would win the 100 metres. I practised every evening in the colony with Appa timing me. Then the whistle went and Sarika was already ahead, and I could see her plait bouncing the whole way. I came third. THIRD.
My face went so hot. Everybody was clapping for her and I felt the tears coming, so I ran to the girls' toilet and stayed there till the relay was over.
I told Meenal the whistle was late for our side. It WAS late, I think. Maybe.
Appa asked in the car and I said I don't want to talk. I didn't eat the laddoo Amma kept for me 😢
I'm never running again.
— Lavanya

qa.q: Where did Lavanya go when she felt the tears coming?
qa.a: She ran to the girls' toilet and stayed there till the relay was over.

qa.q: How can you tell how hurt and upset Lavanya felt?
qa.a: Her face went hot, she hid until the relay was over, she refused to talk and even skipped the laddoo.

qa.q: How could Lavanya's Appa or Amma help her at this early moment?
qa.a: They could sit with Lavanya, say it's okay to feel upset, and not argue about the whistle yet, so Lavanya feels safe to cry and talk later.

qa.q: How might Sarika have felt if she heard Lavanya blame the whistle?
qa.a: Sarika might feel hurt or confused, as if her win was being called unfair.

grounding: It shows a child losing a race, feeling heat in the face and tears, then hiding and blaming the whistle.

passage:
The list went up on the notice board outside the headmaster's room just as the school bell rang for lunch. Tanuja pushed through the crowd of girls, searching for her name under 'Kho-kho: block tournament'. It wasn't there. Zeenat's was.
Her ears burned. Her eyes filled so fast she had to look at the floor. Zeenat turned to say something and Tanuja walked straight past her, out behind the grain shed where the goats were tied, and sat on an upturned bucket.
When her friend Rukhsana found her, Tanuja's voice came out rough. 'Sir always picks his favourites. Zeenat's father helps with the midday meal, that's why.'
She knew it wasn't really why. Zeenat was quicker. But saying it made the lump in her throat a little smaller.
From the field came the shouts of the others practising.

qa.q: Whose name was on the kho-kho list instead of Tanuja's?
qa.a: Zeenat's name was on the list.

qa.q: Why did Tanuja blame the teacher even though she knew Zeenat was quicker?
qa.a: Blaming the teacher made the hurt of being dropped a little easier to bear for the moment.

qa.q: How could Rukhsana support Tanuja right now?
qa.a: She could sit with her and let her be upset without arguing, then later, when Tanuja is calmer, talk about what she wants to work on.

qa.q: What is it like for Zeenat when Tanuja walks straight past her?
qa.a: Zeenat may feel her good news is spoiled and worry that she has lost a friend over the team list.

grounding: It shows a child dropped from the team, with burning ears and tears, who hides and blames the teacher for picking favourites.
